Pattinson starred as Bruce Wayne/Batman in Matt Reeves's 2022 superhero film *The Batman*.[163][164][165] Reeves, following Ben Affleck's departure from the role, wrote the character of Bruce Wayne with Pattinson in mind after seeing his performance in *Good Time*.[166] The announcement of Pattinson's casting was met with backlash from some Batman fans, but the ultimate portrayal of the superhero was applauded by critics following its release.[167][168] Pattinson voiced the titular grey heron in the English-language dub of the 2023 Japanese animated film *The Boy and the Heron* by Hayao Miyazaki.[169]


Pattinson is set to star in Bong Joon-ho's upcoming science-fiction film *Mickey 17* (2024), based on Edward Ashton's novel *Mickey 7*.[170]

In January 2020, an HBO six-hour limited series based on the film, with Bong and Adam McKay serving as executive producers, currently in early development, was announced as an upcoming project.[93] Bong has stated that the series, also titled *Parasite*, will explore stories "that happen in between the sequences in the film".[94][95] In February 2020, Mark Ruffalo was rumored to star while Tilda Swinton was confirmed to being cast as the female lead.[96][97][98] In September 2021, Bong served as jury president of the 78th Venice International Film Festival.[99]

In February 2021, Bong said that he had been working on two scripts after completing *Parasite*, one in English and one in Korean, and that he had finished one of the two. <title>Bong Joon Ho</title>
<fragment>

In January 2020, an HBO six-hour limited series based on the film, with Bong and Adam McKay serving as executive producers, currently in early development, was announced as an upcoming project.[93] Bong has stated that the series, also titled *Parasite*, will explore stories "that happen in between the sequences in the film".[94][95] In February 2020, Mark Ruffalo was rumored to star while Tilda Swinton was confirmed to being cast as the female lead.[96][97][98] In September 2021, Bong served as jury president of the 78th Venice International Film Festival.[99]

[edit]

In February 2021, Bong said that he had been working on two scripts after completing *Parasite*, one in English and one in Korean, and that he had finished one of the two. ## Premise

[edit]


</fragment>
<fragment>
It was announced in December 2021 that Apple TV+ had ordered the series, which will be written and directed by Alfonso Cuarón, with Cate Blanchett and Kevin Kline set to star. Emmanuel Lubezki and Bruno Delbonnel will serve as cinematographers for the series.[1] In February 2022, Kodi Smit-McPhee joined the cast while Sacha Baron Cohen entered negotiations for a role.[2][3] Cohen would be confirmed the next month, with HoYeon Jung also added to the cast.[4] In May, Louis Partridge would join the cast,[5] with Lesley Manville joining the next month.[6] Leila George was added to the cast in October.[7]


Filming for the series had begun by June 2022 in Archway, London and finished production in February 2023.[8][9]

**Esperanto Filmoj** is a Mexican-American film and television production company based in Sherman Oaks, California.[1][2] It is owned by film director Alfonso Cuarón.


The name was coined by Guillermo del Toro, who calls cinematography "the new Esperanto". *Filmoj* is the Esperanto word for *films*, and Cuarón has publicly shown his support and fascination for the constructed international language.[3]


An associated company is Producciones Anhelo, owned by Jorge Vergara and Cuarón.


In 2014, the company made its TV show *Believe*, with Bad Robot and Warner Bros. Television.[4] On December 1, 2021, it was announced that Apple would order its commitment for the show *Disclaimer*.[5]

<document>
<title>Disclaimer</title>
<fragment>

In the case of fan fiction, the author will usually give a disclaimer saying that the author of the fan fiction does not, in any way, profit from the story and that all creative rights to the characters belong to their original creator(s).



## See also

[edit]

* Email disclaimer
* E&OE, an initialism standing for "errors and omissions excepted"
* Mandatory disclaimer


## References

[edit]

1. **^** http://www.pillsburylaw.com/siteFiles/Publications/0C62DFD605F0471619ADF0E2E5576E98.pdf Contractual Limitations of Liability, Warranties and Remedies, Shultis, et al, Pillsbury Winthrop Shaw Pittman LLP, 2006
2. **^** Decision G 2/10 of the Enlarged Board of Appeal of the European Patent Office Archived 2011-10-11 at the Wayback Machine, August 30, 2011, Reasons for the decision, point 2.1.
3. **^** Decision G 2/10, August 30, 2011, Reasons for the decision, point 2.2.

</fragment>
<fragment>
Any statement intended to specify or delimit the scope of rights and obligations

"General disclaimer" redirects here. For Wikipedia's general disclaimer, see Wikipedia:General disclaimer. For other uses, see Disclaimer (disambiguation).

![](image) Disclaimers often concern public safety or business relationships, or, as shown here, may be of a personal nature. Publishing disclaimers is an attempt to provide constructive notice to possible claimants.
A **disclaimer** is generally any statement intended to specify or delimit the scope of rights and obligations that may be exercised and enforced by parties in a legally recognized relationship. In contrast to other terms for legally operative language, the term *disclaimer* usually implies situations that involve some level of uncertainty, waiver, or risk.


</fragment>
<fragment>
In estate or inheritance law, a disclaimer (also called disclaimer of interest) is a written document voluntarily signed by an heir to an estate in which the said heir does not accept (disclaims) the part of the estate of a deceased person which the heir is entitled to receive. The disclaimed part of the estate is then inherited not necessarily by a person of the disclaiming heir's choice, but by the next heir in line to receive that part of the estate as if the disclaiming heir were also deceased, either according to the will, beneficiary designation, or the laws of intestacy. Government tax agencies have further rules on such disclaimers. Reasons for such disclaimers may include the imminent death of the disclaimant or the fact that the disclaimant already has enough wealth.



## Literature

[edit]

The all persons fictitious disclaimer is a standard disclaimer used in works of fiction in an attempt to avoid liability for defamation.


</fragment>
<fragment>

A disclaimer may specify mutually agreed and privately arranged terms and conditions as part of a contract; or may specify warnings or expectations to the general public (or some other class of persons) in order to fulfill a duty of care owed to prevent unreasonable risk of harm or injury. Some disclaimers are intended to limit exposure to damages after a harm or injury has already been suffered. Additionally, some kinds of disclaimers may represent a voluntary waiver of a right or obligation that may be owed to the disclaimant.


</fragment>
</document>

<title>Bong Joon Ho</title>
<fragment>

Bong is preparing for a Korean animation as one of his next films. This animation was conceived since 2018 and said it is a Korean project that is a drama genre involving deep-sea creatures and humans.[101]


In January 2022, it was revealed Bong's next film would be *Mickey 17*, an adaptation of Edward Ashton's novel *Mickey7*. Bong was given an advance manuscript of the novel in late 2021. The film, which was written, co-produced and directed by Bong, will be distributed by Warner Bros. Pictures and will star Robert Pattinson, Bong's first collaborations with both.[102] In May 2022, Naomi Ackie, Toni Collette, and Mark Ruffalo joined the cast and the film is entered in pre-production at Warner Bros. Studios, Leavesden.[103][104] In July 2022, Steven Yeun joined the cast. Production commenced on August 1, 2022.[105][106]

Based on my research from both Wikipedia sources and current project updates, here's a comprehensive answer about Alfonso Cuarón's and Bong Joon-ho's work since 2019:

## **Alfonso Cuarón's Activity Since "Roma" (2018)**

### **Major Projects:**
- **"Disclaimer" (2024)** - A 7-episode Apple TV+ series starring Cate Blanchett, Kevin Kline, Sacha Baron Cohen, Kodi Smit-McPhee, and Squid Game's HoYeon Jung
  - **Production:** Completed filming in February 2023 after 230+ days of shooting
  - **Status:** Currently in post-production, targeting 2024 release on Apple TV+
  - **Significance:** This represents Cuarón's first major project since "Roma"

### **Other Work (As Producer):**
- "Raymond & Ray" (2022) - As producer only
- Various executive producer roles on smaller projects

### **The "Hiatus" Context:**
While it appears Cuarón took several years between major directing projects, he wasn't idle - he was deeply involved in:
- Post-production and promotion of "Roma" through 2019
- Developing and creating the "Disclaimer" series (an ambitious project requiring extensive planning)
- Supporting other filmmakers through his production companies

---

## **Bong Joon-ho's Activity Since "Parasite" (2019)**

### **Major Projects:**
- **"Mickey 17"** - Science fiction film starring Robert Pattinson, Steven Yeun, Toni Collette, and Mark Ruffalo
  - **Production:** Completed filming in December 2022
  - **Status:** Originally set for March 29, 2024, but **delayed to 2025** - currently in post-production
  - **Based on:** Edward Ashton's novel "Mickey7"

### **Other Work:**
- **Parasite HBO Series** - Still in development since 2020 announcement
- Executive producer work on various Korean and international projects

### **The "Hiatus" Context:**
The gap between "Parasite" (2019) and his next release appears to be due to:
- The massive success of "Parasite" leading to extensive international promotion
- Priority on quality rather than quantity
- Development time for ambitious new projects

---

## **Comparison Summary:**

**Neither director disappeared** - both were actively working, but on longer-term projects:

1. **Cuarón** focused on television with "Disclaimer" (requiring filming equivalent to multiple feature films)
2. **Bong Joon-ho** focused on a high-concept sci-fi film ("Mickey 17") with complex post-production needs

**The apparent "hiatus" is actually typical for directors of their caliber** - after major Oscar-winning successes, both took time to develop ambitious follow-up projects rather than rushing to capitalize on their fame.

**Current Status 2024:**
- Cuarón's TV series should premiere later this year
- Bong Joon-ho's film was delayed to 2025 but is in final post-production

Both are maintaining their reputations for quality over quantity, which partly explains why they haven't been as commercially prolific as some contemporaries.
